items.q: What is the 50/30/20 rule actually for?
items.a: It's a **starting audit, not a rigid law**: **50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings**. If needs are 59% of a $3,000 paycheck, trim utilities and grocery unit pricing, then reallocate to savings.

items.q: What should be your first savings priority?
items.a: Build an **emergency fund of 3–6 months of monthly needs** before other goals. Use **separate savings accounts per goal** and compare fees, access, and interest.

items.q: What actually drives a US credit score?
items.a: Scores run **300–850** (700+ decent, 800+ excellent). Weights: **payment history 35%**, utilization **30%**, history length 15%, mix 10%, new inquiries 10%. Income does **not** affect score — **low utilization** wins ($100 on a $10,000 limit = 1%).

In Khan framing, **good debt invests in the future** (education, business, researched home); **bad debt weakens stability** (payday loans at **300–800% APR**, credit-card float, non-wealth purchases). Pay the full card balance inside the grace period.

items.q: Why does starting early beat saving more later?
items.a: The Miguel vs Jasmine parable: **$25/mo from day one** beats **$50/mo starting 10 years later** ($168K vs $147K over 40 years). Compound interest favors **time in market** over amount later.

items.q: In what order should you build a financial plan?
items.a: Five-step priority: **budget → emergency fund → SMART goals → diversify investments → review**. Don't invest on a shaky foundation — **save for short-term liquidity**, invest for medium/long-term risk. Grab **401(k) employer match** as free money.

sections.title: Rent vs buy and real costs

items.q: Does buying a house always beat renting?
items.a: Not by default. Worked example: **$400K house**, $100K down, 6% mortgage → ~**$18K/yr** effective buy cost vs **$16K effective rent** when $100K is invested at 2%. Run the math; psychology and assumptions still matter.

items.q: Why is parking cash in a low-rate savings account risky?
items.a: **Inflation erodes cash**: 2% savings with 3% inflation means you're still **losing ~1%/year** in real terms. Banking type and account choice (credit union, online, CDs) change the rate you earn.
Knowing **what you don't know** so you can look it up. This video is a cliff-notes of Khan Academy's ~**30-hour free course** — foundational literacy before any wealth playbook.
